amai.mnemonic_text: Two uprights with a bar across them and one short stroke floating in the middle of the gap. That stroke is a mouthful being held on the tongue, right between the teeth, and nobody is in a hurry to swallow it. You only hold food in your mouth like that when it is <radical>sweet</radical>.

bou-stick.mnemonic_text: One clean vertical line, top to bottom. No hook, no lean, no second stroke to keep it company. It is the plainest mark in the whole system: a <radical>stick</radical> stood on its end, the kind you drive into the ground to mark a spot or prop something upright before it topples.

bun-writing.mnemonic_text: A lid across the top, and underneath it two strokes crossing each other and splaying out at the bottom like arms thrown wide. It is a figure with something draped over its shoulders and a pattern brushed right across the chest — marks made on purpose, meant to be read. Marks put there to be read are <radical>writing</radical>.

dai-big.mnemonic_text: Stand up, throw your arms straight out to the sides and plant your feet wide apart. That is the entire shape: one crossbar for the outstretched arms, and two strokes kicking away underneath for the splayed legs. A person taking up as much room as a person possibly can, because that is how you show someone just how <radical>big</radical> the thing was.

gandare.mnemonic_text: A flat stroke runs along the top and then drops away sharply down the left side, and there is nothing underneath it at all. That overhang is the whole picture: rock sticking out over empty air, with the ground a long way below. Stand under it for shelter or over it for the view, but it is a <radical>cliff</radical>.

hakenobou.mnemonic_text: A single stroke drops straight down and then, right at the very bottom, flicks back up into a tiny hook. That flick is the whole point of it. It is the <radical>barb</radical> on a fishhook, the little backward tooth that means whatever you have caught is not coming off again, however hard it pulls.

hakogamae.mnemonic_text: Three strokes: a lid across the top, a floor across the bottom, and one wall joining them down the left. The right-hand side is simply missing. The whole container has been tipped over so its open mouth faces you, and now it is a <radical>box on its side</radical>, waiting for something to be slid straight in.

hashiru-run.mnemonic_text: A cross of packed earth up top, and underneath it a leg caught mid-stride: the thigh swinging forward, the foot planting hard, the last stroke trailing off behind where the ground is still coming loose. Nobody stands like this. You only ever hold this shape when you <radical>run</radical>.

hiyominotori.mnemonic_text: A lid across the top, then a wide vessel with a bar ruled across its middle and legs under it. It is a narrow-necked jar standing on the floor, sealed, with the line showing how far down the liquid has got. Nobody seals a jar like that for water. It is a <radical>sake jar</radical>.

kanamuri.mnemonic_text: Two strokes only: a short flick going one way and a longer stroke cutting down across it, meeting at a point near the top. It sits on a character like a roof beam laid crooked, or like a hairpin pushed in at an angle. That narrow angled cap is the <radical>chevron</radical> you will keep finding on top of things.

katahen.mnemonic_text: A lid across the top, and below it a stroke that swings out and then hooks hard to one side, with a crossbar cutting through. It is a signpost at a crossroads: the arm juts out and points, and everyone who reaches it has to pick. That jutting arm is telling you a <radical>direction</radical>.

kau-buy.mnemonic_text: A net stretched flat across the top, and underneath it a shell — the old money, before coins. You spread the net, you sweep the shells in, and you hand them over the counter for whatever was on the shelf. Shells going out under a net is what it looks like to <radical>buy</radical> something.

kawa-skin.mnemonic_text: A hand has got hold of a loose flap at the top left, and you can see its fingers braced at the bottom right as it drags downward in one long, steady pull. What comes away in that pull, in a single unbroken sheet with nothing torn, is the hide: the <radical>skin</radical> taken off whole.

kemonohen.mnemonic_text: Three strokes crowded down the left edge: a short flick at the top, then a long stroke dropping and curving, then a leg kicking out. It is a beast in profile, all snout and haunch, pressed up against the side of the character and ready to bolt. Whenever this is on the left, the word is about an <radical>animal</radical>.

konzukuri.mnemonic_text: An eye up at the top, and beneath it a foot planted flat with the heel dug in and the toes braced against the ground. The eye has seen something and the foot has already answered it, refusing to take one more step forward. Fixed there, staring, immovable: this is <radical>stopping</radical> dead.

ma-hook.mnemonic_text: One stroke slanting in from the left, and a second cutting back under it to a point. The two of them close on each other and end in a sharp little beak that turns inward. Push anything past it and it will catch and hold. It is a <radical>hook</radical>, small and mean and perfectly effective.

men-exempt.mnemonic_text: Someone is squeezing out from underneath a heavy lid. You can see the bent head, the body pressed thin as it works through the gap, and two legs kicking free at the bottom. Everyone else is still pinned under there waiting their turn. This one wriggled out and walked off, which is precisely what it is to be <radical>exempt</radical>.

men-face.mnemonic_text: An outer frame, and set inside it another box with a bar ruled across — a mask hung on a wall, with the flat plane of the cheeks around it and the eyes cut into the middle. It shows you nothing of whoever is behind it. All you get is the front of the thing, its <radical>face</radical>.

mi-body.mnemonic_text: A figure drawn side-on: a head at the top, then a torso thickened out through the middle, and one stroke swinging down and away underneath for the legs. It is a person seen as a shape rather than a face — height, weight, the way they carry themselves. The whole physical <radical>body</radical>.

mizukara.mnemonic_text: A nose, drawn as a narrow face with three lines stacked down the bridge of it. When someone here wants to ask who, me?, they do not jab a thumb at their chest the way you would. They lift one finger and point it straight at their own nose. That nose is how you say <radical>self</radical>.

mochiiru.mnemonic_text: A frame with two uprights driven through it and a pair of bars ruled across the middle, dividing the whole thing into compartments. It is a rack, or a printing block, or a set of pigeonholes — some workshop tool that only exists because somebody had a job for it. Made to be picked up and put to <radical>use</radical>.

nijuuashi.mnemonic_text: Two uprights standing side by side with a single bar laid straight across both of them. They are holding it up together, level, neither one taking more of the weight than the other. Two arms raised to carry the same load: <radical>two hands</radical>.

no-slide.mnemonic_text: One stroke, starting high on the right and falling away to the left, thinning as it goes. Nothing interrupts it and nothing catches it at the bottom end. It is a <radical>slide</radical>: set anything down at the top and it is off the left edge and gone before you can get a hand to it.

nogihen.mnemonic_text: A tree standing upright, and laid across its crown one extra stroke drooping away to the left, as if the head of the plant has been bent over by its own weight. That droop is the whole story. The stalk is loaded, ripe and top-heavy and ready for cutting: this is <radical>grain</radical>.

sara.mnemonic_text: A shallow container drawn face-on: two walls, a flat base, and a pair of uprights inside marking the ridges. It is far too shallow to be a pot and far too wide to be a cup. Set it down on the table and put the food on it, because it is a <radical>dish</radical>.

shou-esteem.mnemonic_text: A small mark and a stroke splitting away at the very top, then a lid, and beneath it a mouth set into a frame. It is a shrine front: the roof flared out at the corners, the offering-slot below, and the whole thing raised a step above the street so you have to look up at it. Built to be looked up at, and held in <radical>esteem</radical>.

tsukue.mnemonic_text: A short flat top with one leg dropping straight down at the left and another hooking under at the right. Nothing in the middle at all. It is the plainest piece of furniture anyone ever built: a slab held up on two legs, room enough underneath for your knees. A <radical>table</radical>.

tsume.mnemonic_text: A flat stroke over the top and, hanging beneath it, three short strokes curving down and in. It is a hand held palm-down with the fingers already curling under, about to close on something from above. Not a grip — a snatch. What comes down out of the sky like that is a <radical>claw</radical>.

ukebako.mnemonic_text: Three strokes with the whole top left off: two walls going up and a floor joining them, and nothing at all across the opening. Whatever you drop in from above lands inside and stays put, because there is no lid to get in the way. It is an <radical>open box</radical>, mouth turned to the sky, waiting to catch something.

warifu.mnemonic_text: A short flag of a stroke at the top, then a long one dropping down the right side and hooking inward at the foot. It is a person folded down onto their knees, bowing low. It is also the carved tally-half that an official presses into wet clay to prove the order is genuine. Kneel, and take the <radical>stamp</radical>.

tooth.mnemonic_text: That top grid of tiny squares stacked over one wide flat stroke is a jaw shot straight on: rows of square little teeth wedged into the gum line so tight not even a sesame seed could slip through, a whole mouthful of <radical>tooth</radical>.

not.mnemonic_text: Picture a hooked loop slashed by three crooked diagonal strokes cutting straight through it, like a prohibition sign scrawled in one angry pass — the whole shape shouting <radical>not</radical> allowed, plain and flat.

eat.mnemonic_text: The peaked stroke on top presses down like a straining lid, and the block beneath bulges outward against it — a takeout container packed so full of rice the lid fights to stay shut, daring you to <radical>eat</radical> before it pops open.

beginning.mnemonic_text: Two short strokes stacked at the top flare like a catching flame, and the two legs splayed below are the matchstick still smoking from the strike — the exact instant a fire, and everything after it, gets its <radical>beginning</radical>.

long-stride.mnemonic_text: The single stroke of 廴 drags low then kicks up into a hook, like tracing the sole of a shoe caught mid-step, skidding forward across wet pavement — the whole line reads as one leg frozen mid <radical>long stride</radical>, stretched further than any real step should go.

separate.mnemonic_text: 釆 reads like a hand of rice flung mid-air, its strokes splaying outward in different directions instead of bunching together — every grain sails off on its own path and lands somewhere else on the floor, each one perfectly <radical>separate</radical> from the rest.

family-name.mnemonic_text: Picture 氏 as an ornate wax seal being pressed onto a letter — the top strokes are the tilted stamp handle, and the long hooked tail is the ribbon of wax it drags out behind it, imprinting one unmistakable <radical>family name</radical> across the page.

wind.mnemonic_text: 風's outer stroke curves out then hooks under like a curtain caught mid-billow, the whole panel bulging and snapping taut in one direction — exactly the shape a sheet takes on a clothesline when a sudden gust of <radical>wind</radical> grabs it.

pike.mnemonic_text: Picture 殳 as a spear at attention: the slanted hook on top is the blade tilted for a thrust, the straight drop below is the shaft, and the curved strokes at the base are a fist clenched around the grip. One weapon, angled to strike — that's the <radical>pike</radical>.

first-time.mnemonic_text: 初 splits into two working parts: the cloth folds on the left are a fresh bolt of fabric laid on the cutting table, and the blade on the right is the tailor's knife coming down through it. That first slice into untouched cloth is the <radical>first time</radical>.

nothingness.mnemonic_text: The crossed grid on top of 無 is the charred window frame of a gutted house, and the four dots beneath are the last embers dying out on the floor — everything that once filled those rooms is burned down to <radical>nothingness</radical>, leaving only the empty frame standing.

head.mnemonic_text: The top bar of 疋 sits like a flat helmet brim, and the strokes below curl into a round skull with a jutting chin, propped alone on that single line — nothing else attached, just one bare <radical>head</radical> that rolled off a shelf and stopped there.

sound.mnemonic_text: The angled strokes on top of 音 are a record needle swinging down, and the boxed square below is a speaker cone with the crossbar marking each thump — that needle dropping is the whole scene, one speaker blasting out pure <radical>sound</radical>.

compare.mnemonic_text: Two identical hooked strokes stand shoulder to shoulder in 比, each curling the same way like a pair of fishhooks laid side by side to see whose barb is sharper — that side-by-side sizing-up is exactly what it means to <radical>compare</radical>.

generation.mnemonic_text: 世 draws as three uneven posts skewered top to bottom by one long crossbar — a family photo flattened onto a single rail, grandparent, parent, and child all pinned to the same line of <radical>generation</radical>.

halberd.mnemonic_text: The top of 矛 curls into a wicked hook, the blade, while one long stroke sweeps down and away beneath it, the wooden shaft angled like it's still mid-thrust into whatever just charged the gate. That hooked blade on a shaft is a <radical>halberd</radical>, full stop.

life.mnemonic_text: Three horizontal layers of soil stack up in 生, and one single stroke drills straight up through every one of them, a green shoot forcing its way through layer after layer of packed earth to break the surface — that stubborn first push upward is <radical>life</radical>.

nine.mnemonic_text: 九 shoots out long and straight, then at the last second curls into a tight hook at the bottom right, like a fishing line cast far out and yanked sharply back the moment something bites — that final snap of the hook is <radical>nine</radical>, one short of a full catch.

left-side.mnemonic_text: A log splits clean down the middle, and you're left holding the half with three snapped branch-stumps still bristling out to the left, the spine running straight down your right hand. That splintered off-cut is the <radical>left-side kata</radical> — one half of a broken pair.

stop.mnemonic_text: Trace 已 and the stroke curls round like it means to close the loop, then quits — the line lifting off mid-curve exactly like a parking-gate arm that drops halfway and jams, refusing to swing the rest of the way down. Everything behind it just has to <radical>stop</radical>.

and-yet.mnemonic_text: A flat bar sits atop 而 like a stiff upper lip, with four strokes drooping below it as a long beard someone strokes while stalling for a comeback. Each slow stroke buys one more second before the words finally arrive: <radical>and yet</radical>.

three.mnemonic_text: 彡 is nothing but three diagonal slashes, raked top to bottom like claw marks down a fence post, each stroke a little shorter than the one before it. Count the gouges and you already have the meaning: <radical>three</radical>.

extend.mnemonic_text: 隶 draws a hand at full stretch, fingers hooked forward, closing on a tail that whips away just below it. That final desperate lunge, arm straining past its limit to close the gap, is <radical>extend</radical>.

going.mnemonic_text: Seen from above, 行 is a crossroads: strokes fork left and right like two roads splitting away from a center island. Pick any branch and your feet are already moving before you decide — that's <radical>going</radical>.
